🔎 **ROOT CAUSE FOUND FOR A FAILURE THIS PROJECT HAS BEEN WORKING AROUND SINCE 2026-08-14: `gh` IS A SNAP.**

Anthony, 2026-08-19: *"I'm not sure if this is really a reflow2 thing (maybe it is part of the governance components?) or an agent thing, but I feel like every time we do a tag/release, I see this again (which means we are not capturing failures as feedback)."*

**IT IS NEITHER.** Measured on the dev box the same day:
  · `/snap/bin/gh -> /usr/bin/snap` — gh is snap-packaged (2.74.0, rev 640).
  · Snap confinement gives it its own sandboxed git WITHOUT the `remote-https` helper, which is why gh's LOCAL post-merge sync dies with `git: 'remote-https' is not a git command`.
  · The SYSTEM git is fine: 2.43.0, `/usr/lib/git-core/git-remote-https` present, and `git ls-remote https://...` succeeds under a minimal env. Every `git push`/`git pull` this session worked.

⇒ **A ONE-TIME FIX EXISTS: install `gh` from the official apt repository instead of snap.** Nine years of workaround discipline is not required for a packaging choice.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ HIS SECOND CLAIM WAS HALF RIGHT, AND THE HALF THAT IS RIGHT IS THE USEFUL ONE.

**WRONG — the failure IS captured**, and richly: `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` is an ENFORCED DesignRule whose FIRST measured instance is exactly this, *"`gh pr merge` — FIVE TIMES on 2026-08-14… the merge had already succeeded server-side every time."* It is why this session read `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` after every merge rather than trusting the exit code, and no merge was ever wrongly retried.

**RIGHT — THE RECURRENCE IS NOT ACCUMULATING.** The rule still says FIVE TIMES ON 2026-08-14. It happened at least FOUR more times on 2026-08-19 (PRs #248, #250, #251, #253) and nobody incremented anything. **So the graph holds the LESSON and not the ONGOING COST**, and the question "how much is this actually costing us?" — the question that would have prompted somebody to look at the packaging — was never answerable. That is his "we are not capturing failures as feedback", stated precisely.

⭐⭐ **AND IT CONVERGES WITH AN INDEPENDENT REQUEST THE SAME DAY.** The hxm_program feedback asks for exactly this mechanism, for a different reason: *"A 'sighting' mechanism for DesignRules — 'this rule was observed again in commit X' as a cheap dated append… Pattern recurrence is evidence the rule is real; today the graph can't accumulate that cheaply."* **Two unrelated sources, one day apart, asking for recurrence-as-a-cheap-append on a DesignRule.** One wants it to prove a craft pattern is real; the other needs it to price a recurring failure. Same primitive.

🛑 NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the ophyd-service session's reported `add_decision` status reset has the same shape (a stale or differently-packaged binary rather than a code defect). It did NOT reproduce on 0.36.0 at either the core or MCP layer, checking both the reply and the store — but the version that session actually ran was not asked for.
